text: B Limitations and Future Work [Back to Sec. 7 in the main paper.] Despite the promising performance of continuous dLMs for language reasoning, several limitations remain. In this section, we outline these key challenges alongside promising directions for future research. Inference Speed and Few-Step Trajectory Distillation. Continuous dLM decoding remains slower per generated token at high step counts compared to fully optimized autoregressive baselines. Under low step budgets, DDIM-4/8 exhibits a major performance drop relative to DDPM-256 ( Tab. 1 ). We observe that neither higher-order ODE solvers ( Sec. G.7 ) nor commit-stride sampling ( Sec. G.5 ) fully bridge this gap. To address this, we explore preliminary on-policy and off-policy Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD), observing encouraging performance gains. Significant headroom remains in optimizing PDD head parameterizations, training objectives, and policy learning strategies. Given that standard DDIM sampling with 16 NFEs maintains decent performance, effective distillation holds substantial potential for 4 × 4\times – 8 × 8\times acceleration, leveraging insights from continuous trajectory distillation in visual domains. Beyond PDD, extending trajectory distillation to consistency and flow-matching frameworks provides a promising path toward real-time continuous dLM generation. Finally, since our model involves self-conditioning, how to distill it into the few-step generative model remains an open question. Encoder–Decoder Robustness. We observe that diffusion-based ELBO training tends to collapse the continuous embedding geometry because the readout decoder (the linear logit projection) is trained predominantly to reconstruct clean, final-step token embeddings. Consequently, the decoder becomes hypersensitive to subtle continuous perturbations. This sensitivity becomes severe when latent representations fall out-of-distribution (OOD), which occurs frequently during early denoising stages, low-NFE sampling, trajectory distillation, or aggressive score steering via CFG and ST ( Fig. 15 ). This latent-to-discrete mismatch might induce decoding errors that bottleneck reasoning performance, especially in code generation where a single syntax error yields complete benchmark failure. To mitigate embedding collapse and strengthen decoder robustness, future research could explore auxiliary cross-entropy losses evaluated across all diffusion timesteps or robustify the readout decoder via VAE-style pre-training prior to diffusion alignment. Memory Overhead and Blockwise KV-Caching Dynamics. Operating blockwise continuous diffusion requires evaluating the transformer denoiser across N N reverse steps per continuous block. Although blockwise generation offers parallel decoding potential, repeatedly updating and querying key-value (KV) states across intermediate noise timesteps increases peak memory bandwidth demand compared to standard single-pass autoregressive KV-caching. Optimizing persistent KV-cache management, state-reuse across intermediate diffusion steps, and extending blockwise continuous diffusion to ultra-long context windows ( > 32 ​ k >32\text{k} tokens) remain important systems challenges for future hardware deployments. Reward-Driven Inference-Time Scaling and Post-Training. Both inference-time reward steering and reward-driven post-training remain largely unexplored for continuous dLMs. At inference, our CFG + ST framework extends naturally to reward-model guidance, sequential Monte Carlo over the denoising SDE, and tilted sampling toward verifier-preferred regions. For post-training, continuous dLMs can in principle inherit the RL toolbox developed for image and video diffusion; whether it transfers from perceptual rewards to language verifiers (math checkers, unit tests, preference models) is an open direction. Multimodal Reasoning and Unified Latents. Because the probability-flow ODE is natively well-defined in our continuous formulation, standard continuous image-diffusion techniques such as trajectory matching ( Song et al., 2023 ; Geng et al., 2025 ; Sabour et al., 2025 ; Boffi et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2026a ; Shaul et al., 2026 ) and distribution matching ( Yin et al., 2024 ) can be directly imported into language modeling. Continuous diffusion is a natural fit for unified multimodal generation architectures ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Xie et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) that bridge text with images, video, or audio. Extending Sigma to joint multimodal continuous trajectories presents a compelling path forward.
